paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The work God's people were doing was good, and opposition showed up anyway. First came a friendly offer of help, and when that got turned down, the pressure started (Ezra 4:2-4). Doing the right thing doesn't promise a quiet kitchen, and that's worth knowing before the heat hits.

Notice how the opposition kept coming across the years, and how it changed shape. It started out sounding friendly, then turned to discouraging the people and making them afraid to build (Ezra 4:4). Then came hired counselors from Cyrus down to Darius, an accusation under Xerxes, and a letter to Artaxerxes about Jerusalem (Ezra 4:5-6, 4:11-16). Verse 24 says "the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased," and I think that was heavy for the builders, so I'm not going to joke my way around it.

But read that last verse again, because it gives a time: the work "remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia" (Ezra 4:24). This passage doesn't promise that every stalled project restarts, but it does show that a stop sign doesn't mean the work was wrong to begin with. So keep that apron on, friend, because this story isn't over.
